Package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery

Class QueryProperty

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery.QueryProperty
public final class QueryProperty extends Object
One bean property as BeanQuery sees it: its column name, value type and inferred SearchType, and how to read and write it.

Instances come from QueryModel. The name is the Juneau bean property name, after @BeanProp and the configured PropertyNamer, so it is the name serializers emit. Reads use the getter (or record accessor), else the field. Writes use the setter, else a non-final field.

Example:

QueryProperty age = QueryModel.of(Person.class).getReadableProperty("age"); SearchType type = age.getSearchType(); // NUMERIC Object value = age.read(person);

Since:
10.0.0

  • Method Details

    • searchTypeOf

      public static SearchType searchTypeOf(Class<?> t)
      Infers a column's SearchType from a property's declared type.

      Booleans are SearchType.BOOLEAN; characters are SearchType.TEXT; primitives and Numbers are SearchType.NUMERIC; enums are SearchType.ENUM; dates, calendars and temporals are SearchType.TIMESTAMP; everything else is SearchType.TEXT.

      Example:

      QueryProperty.searchTypeOf(int.class); // NUMERIC QueryProperty.searchTypeOf(Instant.class); // TIMESTAMP QueryProperty.searchTypeOf(String.class); // TEXT

      Parameters:
      t - The property type. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      The inferred type (never null).

    • canWrite

      public boolean canWrite()
      Returns true if the property has a setter or a non-final field.

      @BeanProp(ro) is deliberately ignored: in Juneau it means "parsers must not set this property", and loading a database row is not parsing.

      Returns:
      true if write(Object, Object) is supported.

      public Object read(Object bean)
      Reads the property from a bean.
      Parameters:
      bean - The bean. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      The value. Can be null.
      Throws:
      BeanQueryExecutionException - If the getter throws or the value can't be read. The cause is the getter's own exception.

      IllegalStateException - If the property is not readable.

    • write

      public void write(Object bean, Object value)
      Writes the property on a bean. A null for a primitive property is ignored, so the bean keeps its default.
      Parameters:
      bean - The bean. Must not be null.
      value - The value, assignable to getWriteType(). Can be null.
      Throws:
      BeanQueryExecutionException - If the setter throws or the value can't be written. The cause is the setter's own exception.
      IllegalArgumentException - If bean is null.
      IllegalStateException - If the property is not writable.
